title: Friends/Family of Individuals at Risk of Suicide Training Program
official: A Pilot Feasibility Study of the Friends/Family of Individuals at Risk of Suicide Training Program
summary: The Friends/Family of Individuals at Risk of Suicide Training (FIRST) program is a six-week program designed to provide knowledge and practical skills to help caregivers care for their loved one while also supporting their own mental health and wellbeing during highly stressful situations. Throughout the program, participants will develop skills to better communicate with their loved one, manage emotions, navigate the health-care system, practice self-care in moments where it feels impossible, and set healthy personal boundaries. FIRST consists of six weekly 90-minute group sessions delivered either online via videoconference or in-person in Toronto, Ontario. Each session is facilitated by a clinician and a peer facilitator with lived experience.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Aged 19 years or older
2. In-person (Toronto) and Virtual (Toronto) group: live in the Greater Toronto Area
3. Virtual (National) group: live in Canada
4. Able to communicate in English
5. Self-identify as FF-STB
6. For participants completing the study virtually: Access to a computer, tablet, or mobile phone with a camera and Internet access

Exclusion Criteria: impairment that would limit understanding of the FIRST Program (e.g., under the influence of substances or alcohol during FIRST sessions, cognitive impairment, active psychosis).
